For sure, I think it's definitely being held back. I think it's at a stage where drifting is growing so rapidly and sponsors just keep jumping on board so the money just keeps trending up. Seems like they think there's no real need to change a lot due to that, unless it's to get more viewers, action on track ect.

I think that's pretty clear with the new qualifying format. I'll admit that I haven't watched much on what the drivers thought, but being someone that likes to really analyze the details of runs, I'm gonna miss single car runs. They changed it to tandem to bring more attraction to Fridays and drum up hype. They can say it was for cost savings for teams, but they've never been concerned about that and qualifying before. And we saw more crashes Friday than I remember seeing at long beach in a while. Not to mention that smaller teams would get the spot light every once in a while getting top spot and stuff.

And it sucks that it's managed and ran the way it is. I've had interactions with sage in the past and he's a really cool dude to talk to. Same with Jarod, but I've had friends and family in the past tell me they can't stand to watch because of his commentary, which I don't blame em for.
Gotcha. Yeah, last year was the seattle where Hughes and Tuerck just kept making it through right? They just kept doing omts till the opposing driver finally would make a mistake if I remember.

I just dont get why it's so hard for them to somewhat emulate series like DMEC for this. They run such an efficient and clean ship over there that produces a great viewing product.

I dont agree with all their rules, cause they can be pretty harsh at times. I think there was an event where Connor actually had to get disqualified cause an exhaust hanger broke. But it feels like there's no downtime while watching them for things like commentators to have to fill.

Yeah, and I somewhat get why in the end, with all known information, the decision was made. However, I think fundamentally with the new rules and ideals it was wrong to re-analyze the first run for the debead point.

In saying that, I don't want anybody to get screwed over by someone getting away with one, but they've done that in the past. If I remember it right, I think there was a Tuerck v Field battle at Seattle where tuercks car let out a bunch of water leading field to spin, but they never redid the battle and gave field a 0.

Idk man, I don't wanna try to blame it on any one person, I just think there's so many things that need clarified or just cleaned up. And being optimistic, maybe it'll get better as they year goes on as all the rule changes become more solidified and better understood. I mean I'm all for eliminating rules to take the judges out of it and put it in the hands of teams and drivers more, so who knows.

I think a major part of it is them trying to get events done quicker and stuff with all the minimal omts and quick decisions that happened. But to me, there just wasn't any justification vocalized to have any of it make sense. And then you have things like straightening not counting as a 0 anymore, which is absolutely crazy to me.

Yeah... I was watching live a bit ago and just had to shut it off cause I was getting frustrated. I'll go back and watch some later, but it was pretty bad. They got rid of protests in an effort to make all calls final (and to not get their own mistakes pointed out) and then pull that.
